hindi: अब इसलिए हम 'अपामार्गतण्डुलीय' नामक अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called "Apāmārgataṇḍulīya".
notes: Chapter title: apāmārga (Achyranthes aspera) + taṇḍula + taddhita -īya ('concerning ...'); the exact intended sense of taṇḍula here is uncertain.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus, indeed, said the venerable Ātreya.
notes: ha sma with the perfect is a traditional formula of reported speech.

hindi: अपामार्ग के बीज, पिप्पली, मरिच, विडङ्ग, शिग्रु (सहजन), सरसों और तुम्बुरु ...
english: The seeds of apāmārga, long pepper, black pepper, viḍaṅga, śigru (drumstick), mustard and tumburu ...
notes: Verses 3 to 5 form one sentence; the verb dadyāt is in verse 5. The list items are not explicitly marked as 'seeds of' for all; bījāni is taken with apāmārga and the rest read as the drugs themselves (grammar allows either).

words.gloss: kuṭheraka and phaṇijjhaka (two plants, names kept)

hindi: जीरा, अजगन्धा, पीलु के फल, इलायची, हरेणुका, पृथ्वीका, सुरसा (तुलसी), श्वेता तथा कुठेरक और फणिज्झक ...
english: Cumin, ajagandhā, pīlu fruits, cardamom, hareṇukā, pṛthvīkā, surasā (basil), śvetā, and kuṭheraka and phaṇijjhaka ...
notes: Edition footnote: another reading has 'ca ajamodām ca' (and celery/ajamodā) in place of 'ca ajagandhām ca'. Identifications of ajagandhā, hareṇukā, pṛthvīkā, śvetā, kuṭheraka, phaṇijjhaka are left unstated here; ajājī is read as cumin (white cumin). The list continues into the following verses (the governing verb comes in verse 5).

hindi: शिरीष के बीज, लहसुन, दोनों हल्दियाँ, दोनों नमक, ज्योतिष्मती और सोंठ — इनका प्रयोग शिरोविरेचन (शिर के शोधन) में करना चाहिए।
english: Śirīṣa seed, garlic, the two turmerics, the pair of salts, jyotiṣmatī and dry ginger: one should give these in head-purging (śīrṣavirecana).
notes: 'Two turmerics' and 'pair of salts' are traditionally haridrā/dāruharidrā and two named salts, but the text does not name them here. The verb dadyāt governs the lists of verses 3 to 5. The verb dadyāt also governs the lists of verses 3 and 4.

hindi: सिर में भारीपन, सिर के शूल, पीनस, अर्धावभेदक, कृमिरोग, अपस्मार, घ्राणनाश (गन्ध का न आना) तथा प्रमोहक (मूर्च्छा/मोह) में —
english: In heaviness and pain of the head, in pīnasa (nasal affliction), in ardhāvabhedaka (half-headache), in worm disease, in epilepsy (apasmāra), in loss of smell and in pramohaka (fainting, bewilderment) ...
notes: Continues from verse 5: these are the conditions for the head-purging drugs. Rendering of pramohaka is literal ('bewildering'); the exact condition is not defined in the verse.

hindi: मदन, मधुक, नीम, जीमूत, कृतवेधन, पिप्पली, कुटज, इक्ष्वाकु, इलायची और धामार्गव ...
english: Madana, madhuka, neem, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana, pippalī, kuṭaja, ikṣvāku, cardamom and dhāmārgava ...
notes: Sentence is completed in verse 8 (vamanārtham prayuñjīta). Compound read as pippalī-kuṭaja-ikṣvākūṇi with final neuter plural; madhuka, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana and dhāmārgava left as names.

words.gram: pres. part. m. nom. sg., a- + caus. √duṣ

hindi: जब कफ और पित्त उपस्थित हों और रोग आमाशय में स्थित हो, तब वैद्य शरीर को हानि पहुँचाए बिना वमन के लिए प्रयोग करे।
english: When Kapha and Pitta are aroused and the disease is seated in the stomach (āmāśaya), the physician should administer for the purpose of emesis, without harming the body.
notes: No object of prayuñjīta is stated; the drugs of verse 7 are understood from context.

hindi: त्रिवृत्, त्रिफला, दन्ती, नीलिनी, सप्तला, वचा, कम्पिल्लक, गवाक्षी, क्षीरिणी और उदकीर्यका ...
english: Trivṛt, triphalā, dantī, nīlinī, saptalā, vacā, kampillaka, gavākṣī, kṣīriṇī and udakīryakā ...
notes: Several of these plants have disputed identifications; names are kept. Reading 'udakīryakām' taken as udakīryā + ka (same plant). Sentence is completed in verse 10 (virekārtham prayojayet).
lines_iast: trivṛtāṃ triphalāṃ dantīṃ nīlinīṃ saptalāṃ vacām
lines_deva: त्रिवृतां त्रिफलां दन्तीं नीलिनीं सप्तलां वचाम्

hindi: पीलु, आरग्वध, द्राक्षा, द्रवन्ती और निचुल — जब दोष पक्वाशय में पहुँच गया हो, तब विरेचन के लिए इनका प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
english: Pīlu, āragvadha, grape, dravantī and nicula: when the doṣa has gone to the pakvāśaya (the lower gut, seat of digested matter), one should administer these for purgation.
notes: Verses 9 and 10 form one sentence. 'pakvāśaya' rendered as the lower gut, its usual sense.

hindi: पाटला, अग्निमन्थ, बिल्व, श्योनाक, कश्मर्य (गम्भारी), शालपर्णी, पृश्निपर्णी और निदिग्धिका ...
english: Pāṭalā, agnimantha, bilva, śyonāka, kāśmarya, śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī and nidigdhikā ...
notes: Edition footnote: another reading 'pāṭaliṃ' for 'pāṭalāṃ'. Verses 11 to 13 form one list governed by 'yuñjyāt' in verse 13. Sentence is completed in verse 13 (yuñjyāt).
lines_iast: pāṭalāṃ cāgnimanthaṃ ca bilvaṃ śyonākameva ca
lines_deva: पाटलां चाग्निमन्थं च बिल्वं श्योनाकमेव च

words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi (sahārtha), adj. of eraṇḍam: 'with punarnavā'

hindi: बला, गोखरू, बृहती, पुनर्नवा सहित एरण्ड, जौ, कुलथी, बेर, गिलोय और मदन के फल ...
english: Balā, śvadaṃṣṭrā, bṛhatī, castor together with punarnavā, barley, horse gram, jujube fruits, guḍūcī and madana fruits ...
notes: 'sapunarnavam' could also mean 'the castor with punarnavā'; both agree with the rendering. Identifications are conventional. The list continues into verse 13.
lines_iast: yavān kulatthān kolāni guḍūcīṃ madanāni ca
lines_deva: यवान् कुलत्थान् कोलानि गुडूचीं मदनानि च

hindi: पलाश, कत्तृण, तथा स्नेह (तेल-घी आदि) और नमक — उदावर्त और विबन्ध (मल का रुकना) में आस्थापन (काढ़े की बस्ति) के लिए इनका प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
english: Palāśa, kattṛṇa, and oils/fats and salts: one should use these in udāvarta and in obstructions, and in āsthāpana enemas.
notes: 'vibandheṣu' rendered 'obstructions' (retention of stool or wind); 'in āsthāpana' may be read as 'for āsthāpana enemas'. The verb yuñjyāt also governs the lists of verses 11 and 12.
lines_iast: palāśaṃ kattṛṇaṃ caiva snehāṃśca lavaṇāni ca
lines_deva: पलाशं कत्तृणं चैव स्नेहांश्च लवणानि च

hindi: इसी औषधगण से वातनाशक अनुवासन (तैलबस्ति) की कल्पना करनी चाहिए। इस प्रकार पञ्चकर्म सम्बन्धी संग्रह कहा गया।
english: From this same group of drugs, the anuvāsana (oil enema) should be prepared, as one that destroys wind. Thus has been stated the compendium relating to the five procedures (pañcakarma).
notes: 'mārutaghnam' may qualify anuvāsanam (taken here) or be read as a separate statement; sense is the same.

words.gloss: of those whose doṣas are aroused

hindi: वे (द्रव्य): जिनके दोष उपस्थित हों उनके लिए स्नेहन और स्वेदन के प्रबन्ध द्वारा, मात्रा और काल का विचार करते हुए, पाँचों कर्म करे।
english: Those (drugs): for those whose doṣas are aroused, by the provision of oleation and sudation, one should perform the five procedures, considering dose and time.
notes: The case of 'tāni' is ambiguous (drugs as instruments or as objects); rendered as 'using these'. The phrase 'after' for the instrumental snehasvedopapādanaiḥ is interpretive; literally 'by means of provision of oleation and sudation'.

words.gloss: having dose and time as its basis
of those possessing knowledge of substances

hindi: युक्ति मात्रा और काल पर आश्रित है और सिद्धि युक्ति में प्रतिष्ठित है। युक्ति को जानने वाला द्रव्यों का ज्ञान रखने वालों से सदा ऊपर रहता है।
english: Yukti (rational planning) rests on dose and time, and success is established in yukti. The one who knows yukti always stands above those who have knowledge of substances.

text_flags.why: stray punctuation mark inside the token

notes: Literally 'those possessing knowledge of substances'.

hindi: इसके बाद मैं नाना औषधों वाली यवागुओं का वर्णन करूँगा, जो उनसे साध्य अनेक विकारों की निवृत्ति के लिए हैं।
english: Next I shall describe gruels (yavāgū) made with various drugs, for the relief of the various disorders that are curable by them.
notes: 'tat-sādhyānām' read as 'curable by those (gruels)'.

hindi: पिप्पली, पिप्पलीमूल, चव्य, चित्रक और सोंठ से बनाई हुई यवागू दीपन (अग्नि को प्रदीप्त करने वाली) और शूलनाशक होती है।
english: A gruel prepared with pippalī, pippalīmūla, cavya, citraka and dry ginger is an appetizer (kindler of digestion) and relieves pain.
notes: One long dvandva (five members) in the instrumental plural; the verb is syāt, upasādhitā is a participle.

hindi: दधित्थ (कैथ), बिल्व, चाङ्गेरी, तक्र (छाछ) और अनार के साथ पकाई हुई पेया पाचन करने वाली और ग्राही (मल को बाँधने वाली) होती है; वात से युक्त अवस्था में पञ्चमूल से बनी पेया (हितकर है)।
english: Gruel cooked with wood-apple (dadhittha), bilva, cāṅgerī, buttermilk and pomegranate is digestive and binding; in a condition accompanied by Vāta, [it is] gruel made with the five roots (pañcamūla).
notes: Subject (yavāgū/peyā) is understood from the preceding verses. 'dadhittha-bilva-cāṅgerī-takra-dāḍima-sādhitā' read as one compound. 'pañcamūla' is not specified in this verse (which group of five roots is left unstated here).

words.gloss: for those with diarrhoea due to Pitta and Kapha

hindi: शालपर्णी, बला, बिल्व और पृश्निपर्णी के साथ पकाई हुई तथा अनार से खट्टी की हुई पेया पित्त और कफ से होने वाले अतिसार वालों के लिए हितकर है।
english: Gruel cooked with śālaparṇī, balā, bilva and pṛśniparṇī, and soured with pomegranate, is beneficial for those suffering from diarrhoea (atisāra) due to Pitta and Kapha.
notes: 'pittaśleṣmātisāriṇām' could also be read as 'those with diarrhoea involving Pitta and Śleṣman'; same sense.

hindi: बकरी के दूध में, जिसमें आधा जल मिला हो, ह्रीवेर, उत्पल और सोंठ के साथ तथा पृश्निपर्णी के साथ पकाई हुई पेया रक्तातिसार (रक्त सहित अतिसार) को नष्ट करने वाली है।
english: Gruel cooked in goat's milk with half water, with hrīvera, utpala and dry ginger (nāgara), and also with pṛśniparṇī, destroys diarrhoea with blood.
notes: 'cchāge' is chāge (the doubled c is an optional sandhi (padāntād vā) after the long final e). 'ardhodake' could also mean 'in milk with half water' (bahuvrīhi qualifying the milk); sense is the same. 'utpala' is left unidentified (several water plants are so called).

hindi: आम की अवस्था में अतिविषा सहित, खट्टे द्रव्य सहित और सोंठ सहित पेया देनी चाहिए; मूत्रकृच्छ्र (कष्टपूर्वक मूत्र) में श्वदंष्ट्रा और कण्टकारी से (सिद्ध) तथा फाणित सहित पेया देनी चाहिए।
english: In the condition with āma, one should give gruel with ativiṣā, with a sour ingredient and with dry ginger; in painful urination (mūtrakṛcchra), gruel prepared with śvadaṃṣṭrā and kaṇṭakārī and with phāṇita (inspissated cane juice).
notes: 'dadyāt' governs both halves; 'sādhitām' (cooked) is understood with the instrumental 'śvadaṃṣṭrākaṇṭakārībhyām'. The edition records a variant 'peyām āme' for 'peyāṃ sāme'. Which 'sour' ingredient is meant is not stated.
lines_iast: dadyāt sātiviṣāṃ peyāṃ sāme sāmlāṃ sanāgarām
lines_deva: दद्यात् सातिविषां पेयां सामे साम्लां सनागराम्

words.gloss: with viḍaṅga, pippalī root and śigru

hindi: विडङ्ग, पिप्पलीमूल, शिग्रु और मरिच के साथ तक्र (छाछ) में पकाई हुई, सुवर्चिका सहित यवागू कृमिनाशक होती है।
english: A yavāgū (thick gruel) cooked in buttermilk with viḍaṅga, pippalī root, śigru and pepper, together with suvarcikā, would be worm-destroying.
notes: The edition records Gaṅgādhara's remark that here buttermilk is to be understood in place of water. 'suvarcikā' is left untranslated (identity not certain). 'krimi' as in the source (usual spelling kṛmi).

hindi: मृद्वीका (द्राक्षा), सारिवा, लाजा (खील), पिप्पली, मधु और सोंठ से (बनी यवागू) प्यास को शान्त करने वाली है; और सोमराजी के साथ पकाई हुई (यवागू) विष का नाश करने वाली है।
english: [The yavāgū made] with grapes (mṛdvīkā), sārivā, parched rice, long pepper, honey and dry ginger removes thirst; and that cooked with somarājī destroys poison.

text_flags.why: possible: lāja requires long ā after sārivā by sandhi (sārivā + lāja = sārivālāja); source has short a (metre unaffected)

notes: Reading of 'mṛdvīkāsārivālaja...' as mṛdvīkā + sārivā + lāja (not 'sārivāla'); source has short a in -vālaja-, flagged as possible error. 'ca' links the two halves of the sentence. somarājī and sārivā are kept as names.

hindi: वराह (सूअर) के निर्यूह (क्वाथ) में पकाई हुई यवागू बृंहणी (पुष्टिकारक) मानी गई है; भुने हुए गवेधुक की (यवागू) मधु सहित कर्शन करने वाली (दुर्बल करने वाली) होती है।
english: A yavāgū cooked in a broth (niryūha) of boar is considered nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa); that of roasted gavedhukā, with honey, is reducing (karśana, slimming).
notes: 'niryūha' = decoction/broth; here of boar (meat). 'yavāgū' is understood with the second half.

words.gloss: in a decoction of kuśa and āmalaka

hindi: घी वाली, बहुत तिल वाली और नमक सहित (यवागू) स्नेहन करने वाली है; कुश और आमलक के क्वाथ में (पकाई हुई) श्यामाक (साँवा) की (यवागू) विरूक्षण करने वाली (रूखा करने वाली) है।
english: [A yavāgū] with ghee, much sesame and salt is oleating (snehanī); [that] of śyāmāka millet [cooked] in a decoction of kuśa and āmalaka is drying (virukṣaṇī).
notes: The input flag mentions a stray '&' before a word (removed by the tool); no change in the token list is needed. 'kuśāmalaka' read as kuśa + āmalaka; it could alternatively be a single name, but the usual reading is two ingredients.
src_flags: source has stray "&" before a word; removed, check word division

words.gloss: removing cough, hiccup, breathlessness and Kapha
removing pain of the pakvāśaya (lower gut)

hindi: दशमूल के साथ पकाई हुई (यवागू) खाँसी, हिचकी, श्वास और कफ को दूर करने वाली है; यमक में मदिरा के साथ पकाई हुई (यवागू) पक्वाशय की पीड़ा को दूर करने वाली है।
english: [A yavāgū] cooked with the ten roots (daśamūla) removes cough, hiccup, breathlessness and Kapha; [one prepared] in yamaka and cooked with madirā (spirituous drink) removes pain in the pakvāśaya (lower gut).
notes: 'yamake' is read as 'in yamaka' (commonly understood as a combination of ghee and oil; not defined in this text); the edition gives no further detail, and the syntax of 'yamake madirāsiddhā' could be taken differently. Kapha is the last member of the first compound.

hindi: शाक, मांस, तिल और माष के साथ पकाई हुई (यवागू) मल को बाहर निकालती है; जामुन और आम की गुठली, कैथ, खट्टे द्रव्य और बिल्व के साथ (पकाई हुई) संग्राही (मल को रोकने वाली) मानी गई है।
english: [A yavāgū] cooked with vegetables, meats, sesame and black gram (māṣa) expels the stool; [one cooked] with the stones of jambu and mango, wood-apple, a sour ingredient and bilva is considered binding.
notes: 'jambvāmrāsthi...' could be 'jambu, āmra-asthi, ...' (stone only of mango) or 'stones of jambu and mango'; 'amla' might be a separate sour ingredient or an adjective of dadhittha or bilva. 'yavāgū' is understood as subject.

words.gloss: moving Vāta downward/in its proper course

hindi: क्षार, चित्रक, हींग और अम्लवेतस के साथ (पकाई हुई यवागू) भेदन करने वाली मानी गई है; अभया (हरीतकी), पिप्पलीमूल और सोंठ के साथ (पकाई हुई) वात का अनुलोमन करने वाली है।
english: [A yavāgū cooked] with alkali (kṣāra), citraka, asafoetida and amlavetasa is considered purgative (bhedinī); [one cooked] with abhayā, pippalī root and dry ginger makes Vāta move in its proper course.
notes: The edition records a variant '-bilvai-' (iti pā-, probably a variant reading) at the end of this line; presumably in place of -viśvair-, but this is a guess. 'anulomana' = setting Vāta moving in the natural direction.

words.gloss: remover of the mishaps/disorders from ghee

hindi: तक्र में पकाई हुई यवागू घृत के व्यापद् (विकार) को नष्ट करने वाली होगी; तक्र और पिण्याक (तेल निकलने के बाद की खली) के साथ पकाई हुई (यवागू) तैल के व्यापद् में प्रशस्त है।
english: A yavāgū cooked in buttermilk would remove the ill effects (vyāpad) of ghee; one cooked with buttermilk and piṇyāka (oil-cake) is recommended in the ill effects of oil.
notes: 'vyāpad/vyāpatti' = mishap or disorder arising from improper use. 'piṇyāka' = residue left after pressing oil (usually of sesame).

hindi: गौ के मांस-रसों के साथ और खट्टे द्रव्य सहित (पकाई हुई यवागू) विषमज्वर का नाश करने वाली है; यमक में पिप्पली और आमलक के साथ पकाई हुई जौ की (यवागू) कण्ठ के लिए हितकर है।
english: [A yavāgū] cooked with broths of cow's meat (gavya-māṃsa) and with a sour ingredient destroys irregular fever (viṣama-jvara); [that] of barley in yamaka, cooked with long pepper and āmalaka, is good for the throat.
notes: 'gavya-māṃsa' literally 'meat of the cow/ox'; commentators may understand it differently. 'kaṇṭhya' = beneficial to the throat (or voice). 'yamaka' is commonly understood as a combination of ghee and oil; not defined in this text.

words.gloss: in the broth of the cock
removing pain of the seminal passage

hindi: ताम्रचूड (मुर्गे) के रस/शोरबे में पकाई हुई (यवागू) शुक्र-मार्ग की पीड़ा को दूर करने वाली है; माष की दाल के साथ घी और दूध में पकाई हुई (यवागू) वृष्य (वीर्यवर्धक) है।
english: [A yavāgū] cooked in the broth of the cock (tāmracūḍa, 'copper-crested') removes pain in the seminal passage; [one] with split black gram (māṣa), cooked with ghee and milk, is aphrodisiac (vṛṣya).
notes: 'retomārga' literally 'passage of semen'. Source spells it retomārga, standard sandhi of retas + mārga.

words.gloss: with apāmārga, milk and the broth of godhā (monitor lizard)

hindi: उपोदिका और दही के साथ पकाई हुई (यवागू) मद (नशे) का नाश करने वाली है; अपामार्ग, दूध और गोधा (गोह) के रस के साथ पकाई हुई (यवागू) भूख को नष्ट कर दे।
english: [A yavāgū] cooked with upodikā and curd destroys intoxication (mada); [one] cooked with apāmārga, milk and the broth of the godhā (monitor lizard) would destroy hunger.
notes: 'apāmārgakṣīra' could mean milk of the apāmārga plant (latex) rather than 'apāmārga and milk'; the dvandva reading is taken as the plain reading. 'kṣudhaṃ hanyāt' is literally 'would kill hunger'; whether this is meant for excessive hunger is not stated here.

hindi: ये अट्ठाईस यवागू कही गई हैं; और पाँच कर्मों (पञ्चकर्म) का आश्रय लेकर औषधों का संग्रह कहा गया है।
english: These twenty-eight yavāgūs have been enumerated; and, having relied on the five karmas (pañcakarma), the compendium of remedies has been stated.
notes: 'aṣṭāviṃśati' = 28; the verse is the summary of the yavāgū list. 'pañcakarma' (five karmas) is kept as in the text; the verse itself does not list them. 'ca' placed after pañcakarmāṇi in the compound 'cāśritya' (pañcakarmāṇi ca āśritya).

words.gloss: for the sake of knowing roots and fruits
for the sake of knowledge dependent on the five karmas

hindi: जो औषध पहले मूल और फल के ज्ञान के लिए कही गई थी, वह पाँच कर्मों पर आश्रित ज्ञान के लिए फिर से कही गई है।
english: The medicine that was stated earlier for the sake of knowledge of roots and fruits has been told again for the sake of knowledge that rests on the five karmas.
notes: 'hetoḥ' is the genitive/ablative used as 'for the sake of' (a postposition-like use). 'mūla-phala' refers to an earlier statement (probably the root and fruit drug groups of Sū. 1); not stated here.

hindi: स्मृतिमान्, हेतु और युक्ति को जानने वाला, जितात्मा (आत्म-संयमी) और प्रतिपत्तिमान् (कर्म में कुशल) वैद्य औषधों के संयोगों से चिकित्सा करने योग्य होता है।
english: A physician who is mindful, who knows cause and rational application, who has mastered himself and is resourceful, is fit to carry out treatment by combinations of medicines.

text_flags.why: 'O' is evidently a data-entry error for 'ño' (hetuyuktijño jitātmā); the metre (16 syllables) and sense confirm it

notes: 'hetuyukti' may also be taken as 'hetu and yukti' (cause and logic); 'pratipatti' = understanding/resourcefulness in action.
